Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:15: And in the Zohar (Parashat Tzav, beginning of 31b) it explains "they defile him from above" to mean that literally, from above, they cause impurity to flow upon him. In these words: it is written, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" (Leviticus 11:44) — whoever sanctifies himself from below, they sanctify him from above; whoever defiles himself from below, they defile him from above. That they sanctify him from above is fitting, for the holiness of his Master rests upon him; but as for defiling him — from where? And if you say from above, does impurity then rest above? Rabbi Chiya said, this is what we have learned: an action below arouses an action above. If the action is one of holiness, it arouses holiness above, which comes and rests upon him and he becomes sanctified by it; and if he defiles himself below, he arouses a spirit of impurity above, which comes and rests upon him and he becomes defiled by it — for the matter depends on the deed, since there is no good and evil, holiness and impurity, that does not have a root and source above; and through the deed below, the corresponding deed above is aroused — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:16: It may also be explained in a second way, which is somewhat close to the previous approach, and I have seen fit to elaborate on it because of the benefits that will flow from it for the practical matter of holiness. "If a person sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him a great deal" — in the Gate of Awe, chapter 5, and the Gate of Love, chapter 3, we explained two matters concerning this; but in order to tie the whole passage together, it appears that the intent follows what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Avot 4:2), "one mitzvah draws another mitzvah," and so on. Behold, at the start of the matter it is little — one mitzvah — and since the first draws a second, and the second a third, and the third a fourth, and so on without end, it follows that the holiness multiplies; therefore "they sanctify him a great deal," in that holinesses from many commandments come into his hand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:17: "From below," "they sanctify him from above" — all the pleasures of this world are drawn from the kelipot, there in the lower Asiyah, as is explained in the Zohar; and behold, a person is equal, in the matter of eating, drinking, and marital relations, to an animal, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in tractate Chagigah (16a): there are six things said of human beings, three like the ministering angels and three like an animal — they walk upright, and speak the Holy Tongue, and possess knowledge and understanding like the ministering angels; and three like an animal — they eat and drink, and reproduce, and excrete waste like an animal — so far their words. Now, a person's walking upright, and likewise his excreting waste, are not within his control, for this is human nature from Adam onward; but the matters of eating, drinking, and procreation, in which he is equal to an animal, require that he sanctify himself, and not eat merely to fill his desire like an animal, and not be likened to the spirit of an animal that goes downward to the earth — and likewise regarding procreation. It says that if he sanctifies himself from all the things that are below, like the animals defiled by the kelipot — as is explained in Parashat Pekudei regarding the chambers of impurity, which by many things lead people astray with the pleasures of the world — they sanctify him above, that is, they say of him and proclaim in all the firmaments, "So-and-so is holy, and no impure thing shall come near him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:18: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar Parashat Pekudei 225b), that wherever there is holiness, the kelipah does not touch, in these words: All the creatures of the world are recognized above, whether on this side or on the other side; those of the side of holiness are recognized above, toward it, and the watchfulness of that side is upon them; and those of the impure side are recognized toward it, and its watchfulness is always upon them. And in a place where the watchfulness of the side of holiness rules, the other side does not watch over it and cannot come near it at all, and cannot push him from his place in anything he does. Concerning this it says, "The eyes of the Lord are toward the righteous..." (Psalms 34:16), because the other side cannot rule over him — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:19: Further, "they sanctify him from above" may also mean that when his soul ascends every night, it ascends to a place of holiness, and the impure ones do not touch it — which is not so for other people, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha 83a) on the verse "My soul yearns for You in the night" (Isaiah 26:9), at length. And further, in Parashat Chayei Sarah (130a), in these words: Come and see, it has already been stated that even in this world, when a person sleeps in his bed and the souls need to roam the world and go forth from the body, not every single soul ascends and roams to see the glorious visage of the Ancient of Days; rather, according to how it is always drawn and according to its deeds, so its soul ascends. And if it is defiled, it sleeps, and the soul goes forth, and all those impure spirits knock upon it and cling to it, among those lower levels that roam the world, and they inform it of things that are soon to come to the world; and sometimes they inform it of false matters and mock it — and this has already been established. But if a person merits, when he sleeps and his soul ascends, it goes and roams and breaks through among these impure spirits, and all of them proclaim and say, "Clear the place, clear it, this one is not of our side" — and it ascends among the holy ones, and they inform it of one true matter — so far his words. And this too is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel 195b), that concerning this it is said, "Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place" (Psalms 24:3) — see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:20: It is possible that regarding this aspect explained concerning "from below," it says in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot 70b), in these words: Rabbi Yitzchak said, fortunate are the righteous in this world and in the World to Come, for they are all holy — their body is holy, their nefesh is holy, their ruach is holy, their neshamah is holy of holies — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:21: Just before this it speaks of the punishment of the wicked, that they become harmful spirits of the world, and afterward it says, "fortunate are the righteous." The reason is that all the evil of the wicked comes to them through the impurity of their body in the desires of the world, whereas all the good of the righteous flows through the holiness of their body, through which they merit a holy nefesh, and so on. Yet even if the vessels of the body's limbs are blemished, even a holy nefesh does not rest in the body, for "whatever has a blemish shall not come near" (Leviticus 21:18). Now, from this passage, we may offer another explanation of "from below, they sanctify him from above" — that they bestow upon him a holy neshamah that comes to him from above, from Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:22: "In this world," "they sanctify him for the World to Come" — meaning that the holiness spoken of is the holiness of all the vessels of the limbs, and their purification from every kind of blemish; yet he still occupies his limbs with worldly matters and commerce, which involves no sin at all, and his thought spreads into the vessels of the limbs to see what they need from the world. But this [third] holiness, which is the holiness of this world, means that he sanctifies himself and separates from the affairs of this world as though he were not a member of this world at all; and this holiness depends on the holiness of thought and its attachment always to the world above. How so? In the previous holiness [level], regarding eating, he separates from excesses and from indulgence, but intends only for the health of his body for the service of the Creator; whereas in this holiness, he intends in his eating that he is eating from the supernal table that is before the Lord, and his sustenance flows to him from the right — and there are several particulars regarding this that will be explained regarding eating, and similarly for all the other particulars of worldly matters. And in his occupation with Torah and commandments, his thought is never for this world, but only to unify [the sefirot] above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:23: It follows that such a person, even though he is in this world, his thought is not in this world but in the World to Come. Therefore "they sanctify him for the World to Come" — that even in the World to Come he is holy, and his level will not be like that of the rest of the people who occupy themselves with Torah and commandments in an ordinary way, whose level is in the lower Garden of Eden; whereas these righteous ones are elevated above, through the pillar in the middle of the Garden, called "mikra'eha." As it is said, "And the Lord shall create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies (mikra'eha), a cloud and smoke by day..." (Isaiah 4:5), and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar Parashat Vayakhel 219a) that this reality is said of the Garden of Eden, and the pillar consists of cloud, smoke, and brightness — cloud and smoke on the outside, brightness on the inside — and he explained the reason why cloud and smoke are on the outside: so that the other righteous ones in the Garden should not see when these ones are elevated above. And "mikra'eha" refers to the righteous who have properly rectified their thought, as is explained there (210b), that through the intention of Torah study and prayer a garment is made for the soul, to raise it up to the upper Garden of Eden — and it is called "mikra'eha," for they are called and summoned to adorn the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:24: And it says there that when these souls ascend above for unification, all the heavenly hosts open at that hour and say, "Fortunate are you, O righteous, keepers of the Torah; fortunate are those who occupy themselves with Torah, for the joy of your Master is in you, for the crown of your Master is crowned through you" — then, once light shines with light, the two lights unite as one and shine; afterward they descend and gaze to delight in the souls of the righteous, and prepare them to be a crown above. Concerning this it is said, "No eye has seen, O God, besides You, what He will do for him who waits for Him" (Isaiah 64:3) — so far his words. And what it means by "once light shines with light" is explained above this, that it is the shining of a direct light from the righteous one, and a returning light from the Shechinah, from the mystery of "female waters" from the righteous — see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:25: It follows that this level of holiness — the holiness of this world, which is the holiness of thought — is greater than the previous one; for the previous one, even though he becomes holy above as explained, does not thereby merit being counted among the "mikra'eha," as explained, whereas this one does merit it. The reason is, "with the measure a person measures, so is he measured" (Sotah 8b): a person who is in this world yet separates himself from this world — whether in solitude, or in his speech, and all the other matters we shall explain in this Gate, please God — is found not to conduct himself in the manner of the people of this world; so too in the World to Come, they sanctify him to be more separated and holy than the rest of the people of the World to Come who are in the Garden of Eden — meaning that he merits to be among the "people of the higher ascent" (bnei aliyah), of whom Rabbi Shimon said, "If there are a thousand, I and my son are among them; and if there are two, I and my son are they" (Sukkah 45b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:26: And in this way it is fitting and precise that it says "in this world" — the intent being that since this world is physical, it is only a temporary dwelling for the soul, which is spiritual; for the soul has no lasting bond or affinity to this world, and the proof is that in the end it removes the garment of this world. Therefore all of one's intent should be toward the essential, spiritual world that comes after this world, which is physical, perishing, and lost. Thus the phrase "this world" indicates two things: first, that it is physical and perceptible, which is [the meaning of] "this," indicating with a finger; and further, that it is not permanent, for after it another [world] will come. Therefore he should truly separate from the acquisitions of the world and its pleasures, and from envy, hatred, and rivalry, and from speaking of worldly matters — for since he thinks he is not a member of this world, he does not speak of it, and all his speech is on the matter of Torah and commandments, which are of the supernal world; and likewise all his thoughts are on the supernal world, which is the essential thing for the soul — for why should he trouble his thought with what will not benefit his soul, but rather, on the contrary, harm it? Therefore it is good for a person, at the time he is occupied with prayer or Torah, to think that he does not stand in this world but in the Garden of Eden before the Shechinah — and by this his thoughts are purified.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:27: This introduction is a key to all the separation (perishut) that we shall explain in this Gate, and I mention it so that we need not repeat these matters each time — for by the reason stated, he will not look at what he has no need for, will not listen to what will trouble him, will not speak [needlessly], and so on, and likewise in his eating and the other matters that will be explained, please God.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:28: In particular, the matter of eating is the greatest for subduing the kelipah in this world and in the World to Come, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah 141a): the bodies of the righteous, who take pleasure in this world only from the pleasures of a mitzvah and the meals of Sabbaths, festivals, and holy times — that impure spirit cannot rule over them, for they take no pleasure at all from their own [worldly indulgence] — so far their words, and the rest of its wording we quoted in chapter 15. This holiness is part of the holiness of this world, included among the other holinesses of this world, and it helps the holiness of the body in the World to Come, so that the spirit of impurity does not rule over it; because the material substance is flesh that draws sustenance from the kelipah, and once one minimizes his eating and takes pleasure only from a meal of a mitzvah, the material substance and the flesh itself become sanctified, and no kelipah rules over it. And certainly he will also need to sanctify his other senses — such as speech, and other pleasures like the pleasure of sleep, marital relations, and the like — for this world is clothed in all these kelipot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:29: Regarding those who sanctify themselves with this holiness, Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Parashat Terumah 151a): for there is no righteous person in the world who does not have the judgment of the grave [i.e., the decomposition of the body by worms], because of [certain reasons], except for those pious ones who stand [firm] in the world, who are worthy to have their soul ascend to their Master, to that supernal place fitting for them — and they are few in the world — so far his words. These are those righteous ones over whom the worm did not rule, because of the proper sanctification of all their senses, in such a way that the kelipah has no portion in them — and this is the holiness of this world, that while they are in this world, they are [already] in the World to Come, as it says, "they are worthy to have their soul ascend to their Master" — and therefore in the World to Come they ascend in level above all the other righteous ones, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:30: When you examine these three divisions we have explained — "a great deal," "from above," "for the World to Come" — you will find them corresponding to nefesh, ruach, neshamah. The first holiness corresponds to the holiness of the commandments that are in Asiyah, corresponding to the nefesh, as explained in the Tikkunim (68b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:31: "From above" corresponds to the ruach, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, likewise explained (Zohar Parashat Vayikra 25a), in the passage we quoted above, when he came to speak of a person's acquiring nefesh, ruach, and neshamah with regard to the level of dreams: he said that when one merits the ruach and ascends above at night, "that ruach goes forth, breaking through mountains and boulders, ascends and spreads out and enters among the holy angels of the world," and so on. And afterward it says, "then this is the bond of a person with holiness." The meaning of "breaking through mountains and boulders" refers to the breaking of the kelipot, called "mountains" and "rocks," as it is written, "And behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind... breaking mountains and shattering rocks" (I Kings 19:11), and my teacher, peace be upon him, explained that these are "mountains" from Samael and "rocks" from Lilith.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:32: And it says, "then this is the bond of a person with holiness" — meaning that this is unlike one who has merited only the nefesh, who is not yet bound to holiness, as it says just before this: and one who has not merited more than the nefesh — that nefesh needs to be rectified to receive the ruach; before it gains that release, what emerges from that nefesh spreads out into the world and wishes to ascend, but is not allowed to until it encounters those [spirits] of the air, who inform it of things, some nearby and some further off, and at that level it goes and becomes attached in its dream, until it acquires the ruach; once it acquires the ruach, and so on. And what it says regarding "those of the air" is explained above this, that they are fine kelipot suspended in the air. It follows that when one merits the ruach, which comes through sanctifying himself below as explained, then they sanctify him from above, meaning he is bound to holiness and has no part in the kelipah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:33: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar Parashat Vayikra 25b) that through the occupation with Torah a person merits the ruach and the neshamah, in these words: Rabbi Shimon said, fortunate are the masters of the neshamah, the masters of Torah, the children of the service of the holy King; woe to those wicked ones who do not merit to be attached to their Master and do not merit [attainment] in Torah, for whoever does not merit [attainment] in Torah merits neither ruach nor neshamah, and their attachment is to that side of evil weapons, and so on. He was precise in his wording, saying "he merits neither ruach nor neshamah," and did not say "he does not merit the nefesh" — for the nefesh is acquired through occupation with the commandments, as is explained in the Tikkunim, in the passage we quoted at the beginning of the chapter, that the positive commandments are in the mystery of Asiyah; but the matter of Torah is through speech, and speech is from Yetzirah, as explained above, "from which the speaking creatures come."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:34: And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar Parashat Bereshit 12b) the commandment to occupy oneself with Torah study — that through occupation with Torah a person merits the neshamah, in these words: the fifth commandment. It is written, "Let the waters swarm with living creatures" (Genesis 1:20). In this verse there are three commandments: one, to occupy oneself with Torah; and another, and so on — to occupy oneself with Torah and to strive in it and to increase it every day, and not to neglect it, as is fitting — for it is written "let the waters swarm," which refers to the Torah, in which one must strive every day to rectify his nefesh and his ruach. For once a person occupies himself with Torah, he becomes rectified with another, holy neshamah, as it is written, "the swarm of a living soul (nefesh chayah)" — the nefesh of that holy "living" [entity]. For when a person does not occupy himself with Torah, he has no holy nefesh, and the holiness from above does not rest upon him; but when he strives in Torah, through the very movement of his lips as he studies it, he merits that living nefesh, and comes to resemble the holy angels, as it is written, "Bless the Lord, His angels" (Psalms 103:20) — these are those who occupy themselves with Torah, who are called "His angels" on earth, and so on. And the conclusion of this passage: concerning this David said, "Create in me a pure heart, O God" (Psalms 51:12) — [meaning] to occupy myself with Torah — "and then, renew a steadfast spirit within me" — so far his words. This makes it explicit that the merit of the holy neshamah, and even the ruach, all comes through occupation with Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:35: And it explains, concerning occupation with Torah, the conditions required of one who wishes to merit the neshamah: first, it says "to occupy oneself with Torah and to strive in it," repeating the wording with "to strive in it," to allude that one must strive to grasp its innermost depth, the depth of the matter he is occupied with, even in a point of halachah, as it is said, "if you seek it as silver, and search for it as for hidden treasures" (Proverbs 2:4). To this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, referred in saying, "Let a person first learn by rote and then analyze it," as it is written, "My soul grasps [gorsah]..." (Psalms 119:20).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:36: And it further says "to increase it every day" — that he should strive to be fruitful and multiply in it; just as one must be fruitful and multiply in the physical sense, so must he be fruitful and multiply in the spiritual sense, and his intellect should not be a barren tree that bears no fruit. This is what they meant by saying (Avot 1:13), "and one who does not add [to his learning], loses [it]" — that a person should not [merely] learn today what he learned yesterday, ending up occupied with a single point of halachah his whole life, entering and leaving the study hall without any new insight; and if, God forbid, he does not add so as to bear fruit, he is like a dry tree that bears no fruit, which is cut down, having no use except as firewood. And it says "every day," for just as the days are renewed, and today is not what it was yesterday — this being what we say (in the blessing Yotzer Or), "and He constantly renews, every day, the work of creation" — so too, every day one should study something new that he did not know previously; and by this the days are found to shine and be rectified, that is, [with] the light of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:37: And it says, "and not to neglect it" — for one who learns and forgets is like one who fathers a child and buries it; and just as with one's physical children, a person does not want to bury them, but wants their existence to endure in the world, so it must be with Torah. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 32b) that the death of children comes because of the sin of neglecting Torah, as it is said, "you have forgotten the Torah of your God, I will also forget your children" (Hosea 4:6). Therefore one must strive to learn something new, that is, to be fruitful and multiply, and to strive to review everything he has learned, so as not to forget it. But one who learns and forgets is not given [further] novelty, so that he not bury [what he learns] the way he buried what came before.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:38: When a person studies Torah in this manner, it indicates his great yearning for the Torah, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, bestows upon him a holy neshamah, and then he is like an angel divested of materiality. The reason that the acquisition of the neshamah is through Torah is that the neshamah's source is above, from Binah, as it is said, "and the breath (neshamah) of the Almighty gives them understanding" (Job 32:8), and the Torah likewise is drawn from there, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayetze); therefore the sustenance of the neshamah is through Torah. And so we find it called "bread," as it is said, "Come, eat of my bread" (Proverbs 9:5); and it says in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, end of 227a) that for this reason one must "grind" the words of Torah — for just as the body is nourished by physical bread after the wheat has been ground, and the bran and chaff and straw sifted out, leaving pure fine flour, so too the nourishment of the neshamah requires the grinding of Torah words; and we shall quote its wording further below, please God.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:39: And so it says in the Tikkunim (49a), that Torah is what gives strength and vigor to the neshamah, ruach, and nefesh, in these words: fortunate is he who unites neshamah and ruach with nefesh through the voice of Torah study, which strengthens them, for whoever does not occupy himself with Torah, his neshamah, ruach, and nefesh are weakened — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:40: Another reason for acquiring the neshamah through Torah: because Torah is acquired through forty-eight things (Avot 6), [beginning with] listening with the ear, and so on — with awe, with limited sleep, with limited indulgence, with limited worldly involvement — for all these preparations are the removal of the love of the world from a person's heart. The reason is that Torah, because of its spirituality, rests upon a person until he acquires these qualities in his heart, and distances himself from the love of the good things of this world, and casts off, as it were, the garment of materiality, until he resembles an angel in the refinement of his soul and body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:41: One might also note the word "is acquired" [used] regarding Torah, which is not used regarding priesthood or kingship — for the wording of the Baraita, as found in our texts, is "Torah is greater than priesthood and than kingship," for kingship [is acquired] with thirty qualities and priesthood with twenty-four, but the term "acquisition" is not used regarding them, whereas regarding Torah it uses the term "acquisition." The reason is that Torah is called "the daughter of the King," and behold, the law is that a woman is acquired (betrothed) in three ways, and "acquisition" is the term for betrothal (kiddushin); so too the reality of the Torah, called "the daughter of the King" — her betrothal, which a person gives her so that she becomes married to him, revealing her secrets to him, is through the forty-eight things mentioned. And when a person merits the Torah by acquiring the things mentioned, he then merits the neshamah — and therefore Rashbi called the possessors of the neshamah "masters of Torah." In these words, in Parashat Vayikra (25b): Rabbi Shimon said, fortunate are the masters of the neshamah, the masters of Torah, the children of the service of the holy King, and so on. And because a person merits the Torah only through action, it says "children of the service of the holy King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:42: And whoever merits the neshamah is the one who merits to unify [the sefirot] above, in the supernal sefirot, and his unification is a complete unification; and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah 141b), of blessed memory, regarding the neshamah — and just before this it explains the matter of nefesh and ruach — it says: the neshamah ascends immediately to its place, to that place from which it emerged, and it is for its sake that the lamp is illuminated, to shine above — so far his words, as far as pertains to our subject. And because the supernal unification is achieved only through proper intentions, and the neshamah rests upon a person only through the acquisition of [proper] thought, therefore whoever has a neshamah is the one who performs the unification and causes the light of the Shechinah to shine above through him. But so long as a person is entangled in matters of materiality, he has no neshamah, and his unification is not a [true] unification.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:43: Regarding the possessors of the neshamah it is said in the passage before us, "if a person sanctifies himself in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come" — and this is the world of thought, corresponding to the neshamah, as explained. It is possible to say that "they sanctify him for the World to Come" means that they bestow upon him the neshamah of Atzilut, for whoever has the neshamah of Atzilut is holy for the World to Come; and this is the very same matter explained above regarding those called "mikra'eha" — and it is impossible to attain that level except through sanctifying oneself by meriting the neshamah of Atzilut, for whoever merits the neshamah of Atzilut has the highest of all levels, as is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra 24), in these words: fortunate are the righteous who have a supernal portion in the Holy One, blessed be He, a holy portion in the holiness of the King, because they sanctify themselves with the holiness of their Master; and whoever sanctifies himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies him, as it is written, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" (Leviticus 11:44) — a person sanctifies himself from below, and they sanctify him from above; and when a person is sanctified with the holiness of his Master, they clothe him with a holy neshamah, the inheritance of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel, and then he inherits everything; and these are called "children" to the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, "You are children to the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 14:1) — and this has already been established — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:44: When you examine the words of this passage carefully, you will find that it mentions the three holinesses stated in the passage of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, that we are dealing with — for it says, "whoever sanctifies himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies him," corresponding to "if a person sanctifies himself a little"; "from below, they sanctify him from above" is explicitly mentioned as "a person sanctifies himself from below," and so on. Corresponding to the third, which says "in this world, they sanctify him for the World to Come," it is precise in saying, "and when he is sanctified with the holiness of his Master" — and this is certainly the holiness of thought, in its separation from all worldly things and its attachment always to the world above, through his intent in the supernal attributes — and this is "the holiness of his Master"; then they clothe him with the neshamah of Atzilut, as explained — so that by this he will be holy in the World to Come, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:45: It is precise in saying "they clothe him," and not "they give him a neshamah," and so on — in light of what was explained above in chapter 2 concerning holiness, that holiness has two aspects: one is the garment made for the neshamah through the drawing down of holiness upon it, and the second is separation, as I elaborated there; therefore it says "they clothe him." And I found something similar in the Zohar (Parashat Chayei Sarah, beginning of 125b), in these words: and therefore, when a person comes to purify himself, they assist him from above, and the assistance of his Master surrounds him and guards him, and he is called holy — so far his words. And from what it says, "surrounds him," it appears to explain that it is like a garment that encircles a person on all sides.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:46: And so it is likewise explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas 245b), in these words: and it says regarding the cup, that it requires rinsing on the outside and washing on the inside; and the secret of the matter is "and he shall purify and sanctify it" (Leviticus 16:19) — purity on the inside, holiness on the outside. And just as the cup's purity and holiness are not [complete] inside and out without water, so too the neshamah's purity and holiness are not [complete] without Torah; and therefore Rabban Gamliel said, "Whoever is not the same inside as outside may not enter the study hall," because he is not from the Tree of Life but from the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil — so far his words. This makes it clear that there is holiness on the outside. And incidentally we learn that a person's acquisition of purity and holiness is entirely through occupation with Torah, as is also explained in Parashat Kedoshim (80b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:47: We thus learn that for a person to cleave to holiness, he must strive to acquire nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, which are acquired through the performance of the commandments, the study of Torah [speech], the purification of thoughts, and the intention behind Torah study and the commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:48: And in Ra'aya Meheimna (229a) it explains that these mentioned [three levels] are also the three Names, Ehyeh, YHVH, Adonai, which together numerically equal 112 (Yavak); and these three Names are the root of neshamah, ruach, and nefesh — whether in the mystery of Atzilut, or below in the Throne, Chayah, and Ofan — namely, Ehyeh is the supernal Imma who nests in the Throne with the three supernal sefirot; YHVH nests in Metatron with the six sefirot; Adonai, the Shechinah, nests in the Ofan — see the Tikkunim (23a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:49: In this same manner it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayera 99a) that for a person to draw holiness upon himself, it is through these three things mentioned — thought, speech, deed — in these words: Rabbi Abba opened, "Who shall ascend the mountain of the Lord, and who shall stand in His holy place" (Psalms 24:3). Come and see: all the people of the world do not see upon what the world stands, and the days go and ascend and stand before the Holy One, blessed be He — all those days that a person exists in this world, for they are all created and all stand above. And how do we know they are created? As it is written, "days were formed" (Psalms 139:16). And when the days come to depart from this world, they all draw near before the supernal King — this is what is written, "and the days of Israel drew near to die" (Genesis 47:29) — because when a person is in this world, he does not take note or consider upon what he stands, but rather every single day he thinks as though he goes about emptily; for when the soul departs from this world, it does not know which path leads it upward — for the path to ascend above, to the place where the light of the supernal souls shines, is not given to all souls, since just as a person draws himself in this world, so is he drawn after he departs from it. Come and see: if a person is drawn after the Holy One, blessed be He, and his longing is after Him in this world, then afterward, when he departs from it, he is drawn after Him, and they give him a path to ascend above, according to that drawing that was drawn by his will every day in this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:50: Rabbi Abba said: one day I happened upon a certain town of the descendants of the East, and they told me of that wisdom which they knew from ancient days, and we found books of their wisdom, and they brought me one book, in which it was written that a person's will, wherever he directs it in this world, so does he draw a spirit upon himself from above, corresponding to that will to which he attaches himself. If his will is directed toward a supernal, holy matter, he draws that matter down upon him from above to below; and if his will is to attach himself to the other side and directs himself toward it, he likewise draws that matter down from above to below toward himself — and they used to say that the root of the matter depends on words, deeds, and will, to become attached, and by this the side to which he is attached is drawn down from above to below. And I found in it all the deeds and services of the stars and constellations, and the matters they require, and how the will should be directed toward them in order to draw them to oneself. In the same way, all those spirits and demons of the impure side [instruct] all who wish to attach themselves to the impure side. Likewise, whoever wishes to attach himself above through the holy spirit — for the matter depends on deed, words, and the intention of the heart to direct itself toward that matter, to draw it toward himself from above to below and to attach himself to that matter. And they used to say: just as a person is drawn from this world, so too they draw him when he departs from this world; and by whatever he attaches himself to and is drawn after in this world, so he attaches himself in that world — if to holiness, to holiness; and if to impurity, to impurity. If to holiness, that side draws him toward itself and he becomes attached to it above, and he becomes an appointed servant, a servant to the [supernal] servant before the Holy One, blessed be He, among the other angels, just as he was attached above, and he stands among those holy ones, as it is written, "and I will give you access among these that stand by" (Zechariah 3:7). Likewise, if to impurity, that side draws him toward itself, and he becomes as one of them, attached to them, and they are called "harmers of humanity"; and at the hour they depart from this world, they take him and defile him in Gehinnom, in that place where they judge the impure ones who have defiled themselves and their spirits, and afterward he becomes attached to them, and he becomes one of those harmers of the world. I said to them, "My children, this is close to the words of the Torah," and so on. And the conclusion of the matter: therefore a person must draw himself after the Holy One, blessed be He, and cleave to Him always, as it is written, "and to Him shall you cleave" (Deuteronomy 10:20) — so far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:51: It is thus made clear that attachment [to God] is acquired through deed, speech, and thought, and the reason, as explained, is that these are the levels of ascending the ladder; and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach 55b), in explanation of the verse, "Do not forsake your own friend and your father's friend" (Proverbs 27:10) — where it explains there that this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He — that attachment to Him, blessed be He, is precise through these things mentioned, and one who performs these does not forsake Him; and we shall quote this passage further below, please God.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:52: Concerning these three things, the Torah said, "For the matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it" (Deuteronomy 30:14) — "in your mouth" is speech, "in your heart" is thought, "to do it" is deed. And concerning these three it is said, "And behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens..." (Genesis 28:12).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:53: And incidentally, this passage makes clear the greatness of the level of attachment to holiness — how great it is, and how much a person is obligated to pursue it — as we have said, that in the manner one attaches himself in this world, so he becomes attached in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 4:54: And with this, this chapter is concluded:
